overall_summary: Crypto is caught in mixed signals with clear bearish pressure from ETF outflows, large Bitcoin movements, and delayed regulation. At the same time, falling yields, a weaker dollar, and Iran de-escalation hopes offer macro support that could limit downside. Near-term direction hinges on upcoming data and whether risk-on flows return.
key_points: Falling yields and dollar support risk assets
Large BTC wallet moves spark sale talk

items.title: Coldcard Exploit Hits $114M as Fourth Sweep Hits
items.summary: A firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets dating to 2021 has enabled multiple waves of thefts, with a possible fourth sweep pushing estimated losses to about 1,816 BTC or roughly 114 million dollars from over 5,200 addresses. Bitcoin slipped under 63,000 dollars even as macro news improved, while smaller holders flooded exchanges with coins in a reverse of the post-FTX self-custody rush. Traders should care because this rattles confidence in cold storage, adds supply pressure via exchange deposits, and keeps a lid on any rebound until the attacks fully stop.
items.impact: Near-term price pressure and risk-off sentiment from eroded self-custody trust

items.title: Senate Skips CLARITY Act Vote With Days Left
items.summary: The U.S. Senate left the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act off Monday's floor schedule, leaving just five days before the August recess. Industry groups and figures like former Defense Secretary Mark Esper are pushing hard, but unresolved fights over DeFi, enforcement, and ethics keep it stalled, with passage odds already cut. Traders should watch this closely because a clean regulatory framework is seen as a major unlock for institutional capital; missing the window delays that catalyst into mid-September or later amid midterm politics.
items.impact: Removes near-term positive regulatory catalyst and extends uncertainty

items.title: Trump Media Moves Another $165M in Bitcoin
items.summary: Wallets tied to Trump Media transferred 2,628 BTC worth about 165 million dollars to Crypto.com, leaving holdings near the 4,261 BTC previously pledged as loan collateral. The company has now moved out over 7,000 of the 11,542 BTC it bought near cycle highs, with analysts estimating hundreds of millions in realized and unrealized losses. Traders care because confirmed sales would add corporate selling pressure, while even custody shifts signal reduced conviction from a high-profile holder.
items.impact: Potential additional supply overhang if transfers prove to be sales

items.title: Strategy Wallet Moves 300 BTC, Sparking Sale Talk
items.summary: On-chain trackers flagged a wallet linked to Michael Saylor's Strategy moving 299.84 BTC worth nearly 19 million dollars, echoing the pattern before its July sale of over 3,500 BTC. The firm has not confirmed any sale and recently highlighted a stronger cash reserve for dividends, while Saylor posted bullish signals days earlier. This matters for traders because Strategy remains the largest corporate holder; any renewed selling would hit sentiment hard after it already broke its never-sell stance earlier this year.
items.impact: Watch for confirmation; unconfirmed move keeps uncertainty elevated

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $265M Outflow on July 31
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly 265 million dollars in net outflows on the last trading day of July, led by BlackRock's IBIT, flipping after prior inflows and contributing to a weak monthly total. Broader recent flows have been choppy with multi-day negative stretches, and traders note thin volume in the current sell-off from 65,000. This is key because ETF demand has been a primary price driver; sustained outflows remove a major bid and signal waning institutional appetite into August.
items.impact: Weakens a core source of institutional buying pressure

items.title: Bitcoin Futures Yields Fall Below Treasury Notes
items.summary: The bitcoin futures basis, once yielding over 20 percent in bull markets, has now trailed two-year U.S. Treasury yields for months, sitting around 3 percent versus 3.8 percent for Treasuries. Futures volumes have slumped sharply as the carry trade loses appeal, a sign of reduced arbitrage opportunities. Traders should note this as evidence of a maturing but lower-demand market; weaker futures activity can reduce leverage and liquidity, making spot moves more sensitive to flows and news.
items.impact: Signals market maturation but also cooler speculative and institutional interest

items.title: US-Japan Confirm First Joint Yen Intervention in 15 Years
items.summary: Japan and the US Treasury confirmed they conducted coordinated yen-buying intervention on Friday, the first joint action since 2011, to counter disorderly moves after the yen hit multi-decade lows near 164. Officials from both sides, including Treasury Secretary Bessent and Japan's finance minister, signaled readiness for more action if needed. Traders should care because this pressures the US dollar lower, eases global financial conditions, and often supports risk assets including crypto by reducing DXY strength.
items.impact: Weaker DXY and improved risk appetite likely lift Bitcoin

items.title: Treasury Yields Fall as Oil Plunges on Iran Diplomacy Hopes
items.summary: US Treasury yields dropped across the curve on Monday, with the 10-year near 4.68 percent and the 30-year easing from recent multi-year highs, as oil prices slumped around 5 percent. The move followed President Trump's comments on restarting talks with Iran and holding off strikes, raising de-escalation hopes that could reopen energy flows. Crypto traders should watch this closely because falling yields and energy prices ease inflation fears and financial conditions, typically bullish for risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Lower yields and oil reduce rate-hike pressure, supporting equities and crypto

items.title: NY Fed's Williams Backs Rate Hold in Fresh Interview
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams, in a Reuters interview released Monday, strongly supported last week's decision to hold rates at 3.5 to 3.75 percent. He said tariff effects on inflation have mostly passed through, Middle East energy risks may have peaked in his base case, and current policy is well positioned for gradual disinflation toward 2 percent by 2028 without overheating. Traders care because this counters the three hawkish dissents and keeps September hike odds in check, favoring a less restrictive path for risk assets.
items.impact: Dovish tilt from key voter reduces near-term hike odds

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI and Key Data Due Today
items.summary: Markets are focused on today's July ISM Manufacturing PMI, expected around 54, along with the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI and construction spending. This follows last week's divided Fed hold and comes ahead of Friday's jobs report. Crypto traders should pay attention because a strong print could reinforce growth and sticky inflation concerns that support higher-for-longer rates, while a soft one might ease pressure and boost risk appetite into the employment data.
items.impact: Data-dependent catalyst for yields, dollar, and risk assets ahead of NFP

items.title: Dollar Index Extends Decline Toward Multi-Week Lows
items.summary: The US Dollar Index fell further on Monday toward the mid-99s, extending a multi-session slide amid the yen intervention, softer yields, and oil drop. It has weakened over 1 percent in the past month. For crypto traders this matters directly as a softer dollar historically correlates with stronger Bitcoin and risk-on flows by improving global liquidity conditions.
items.impact: Weaker DXY typically supportive for Bitcoin prices

items.title: Markets Eye Friday Jobs Report Amid September Hike Bets
items.summary: Attention turns to Friday's July nonfarm payrolls after last week's Fed hold with three dissents for a hike, leaving September rate-increase odds around two-thirds in some pricing. Soft recent payrolls and stable unemployment keep the data pivotal for the path of policy under Chair Warsh. Traders should care because a hot jobs number could cement hike expectations and pressure risk assets, while a cool one would reinforce the pause and support crypto.
items.impact: High-stakes labor data will drive near-term Fed pricing and volatility

items.title: Trump Calls Off Iran Strikes, Talks Set for Monday
items.summary: President Trump said he canceled what he described as a massive planned attack on Iran after regional players signaled parameters of a deal. Talks are set to begin Monday with the goals of fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing Iran's nuclear program. No deadline was given and Iran has sent mixed signals. Traders should care because the strait handles about 20 percent of global oil and LNG; de-escalation hopes have already sent oil down more than 4 percent and lifted risk appetite.
items.impact: Lower oil and geo-risk premium supports risk assets including crypto

items.title: Oil Tumbles Over 4 Percent on Iran De-Escalation Hopes
items.summary: Brent and WTI crude each fell roughly 4.5 to 5 percent after Trump held off fresh strikes and pursued a deal to reopen Hormuz. OPEC-plus also agreed a small September production increase. Shipping data still shows thin traffic and recent tanker attacks, so the calm remains fragile. Energy shocks have driven inflation and risk-off moves all year; a sustained drop in oil would ease pressure on markets and support broader risk taking.
items.impact: Eases inflation fears and boosts risk sentiment across equities and crypto

items.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Deep into Russia, Hit Wildberries
items.summary: Overnight and Sunday Ukrainian drone attacks killed at least eight people across Russian regions and set fire to a Wildberries warehouse far from the front. Ukraine also claimed hits on a Saratov refinery and Engels airbase while Russia said it downed hundreds of drones. These deeper economic and infrastructure strikes raise the chance of wider escalation or retaliation. Persistent war risk keeps energy and defense volatility elevated and can cap risk appetite.
items.impact: Heightens escalation risk and supports safe-haven flows

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill 15 in Gaza Despite Ceasefire Push
items.summary: Israeli airstrikes continued for a second day, killing at least 15 Palestinians according to medics, even after Trump hailed progress on disarming Hamas. An Israeli minister said there is no deal to halt attacks and expressed skepticism Hamas will disarm. The fighting keeps Middle East tensions high alongside the Iran conflict. Ongoing violence adds to regional instability that can spill into energy markets and broader risk sentiment.
items.impact: Sustains Middle East risk premium without clear new directional catalyst

items.title: Ceuta Migrant Death Toll Hits 72 After Mass Morocco Rush
items.summary: The death toll from last week's unprecedented surge of more than 50,000 people into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta rose to at least 72. Most have already returned to Morocco but the crisis prompted Italy to suspend Schengen travel with Spain and drew an EU letter calling for stronger external border measures. Large migration shocks can fuel political instability in Europe. Traders watch for any knock-on effects on EU cohesion or policy shifts that influence the euro and risk assets.
items.impact: Raises European political risk but limited immediate market impact

items.title: EU Boards Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker
items.summary: An Italian-led EU naval force boarded the sanctioned tanker Toa Payoh in the Mediterranean to verify its flag and nationality. The vessel was part of Russia's shadow fleet used to evade oil sanctions. This is part of stepped-up enforcement against vessels helping Moscow fund its war. Tighter sanctions pressure can further constrain Russian energy exports and keep global oil supply tight even as other geopolitical fronts shift.
items.impact: Supports oil prices via tighter Russian export enforcement
